newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish navy ships leave northern Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Turkish navy ships leave northern Cyprus.

text.p: Three Turkish navy ships left northern Cyprus on Wednesday after a five-day visit to show Ankara's solidarity with the breakaway Turkish Cypriot state, state-run Anatolian news agency reported.
Crowds waved Turkish Cypriot and Turkish flags as the frigate and two assault boats left the port of Famagusta in notheastern Cyprus, the agency said.

Turkey has promised closer military and political links with the self-declared Turkish Cypriot republic in response to Greek Cypriot plans to install anti-aircraft missiles from Russia in the south of the island.
Ankara, which has 30,000 soldiers on Cyprus, has threatened a military strike if the deployment goes ahead. The missiles are not expected to be installed for 16 months.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup backed by Athens.
